title: Wild Badger Power 40 Volt Self-Propelled Mower
text:
Why I Tried This Mower
I wanted to see if the Wild Badger Power 40 Volt Self-Propelled Lawn Mower could handle my 1/2-acre lot during the fall. Between grass clippings and leaves, I needed something quiet and cordless to make the job easier.

My Experience
Putting the mower together was quick and easy—no hassles there. It’s lightweight and really easy to move around, but I did notice the plastic wheels slipping on slight inclines, which got annoying. When I used the bagging option, the bag only filled to about 75% before I had to stop and empty it, which slowed things down. Plus, the batteries ran out before I could finish the job, and recharging them took longer than I expected.

When I switched to mulching, things went way smoother. It handled the mix of grass and leaves well, and I was able to finish the whole yard with both batteries.

What It Did for Me
The mower was super quiet, which was great—I didn’t feel like I was disturbing anyone. Mulching saved me time since I didn’t have to keep stopping to empty the bag. On the downside, the battery life isn’t quite enough for my yard when bagging, and the long charging time was frustrating.

My Take
This mower is a good fit for smaller, flat yards. It’s easy to use, does a great job mulching, and is lightweight. But for larger yards or places with inclines, the battery life, recharge time, and wheel traction might be a problem.

Overall, it’s a nice eco-friendly option, but it comes with a few trade-offs if you’ve got a bigger yard like mine.

productName: Cordless 40-volt 20-in Single-stage Push Battery Snow Blower (Battery Included) (Charger Included)
title: Only uses a single battery and has design flaws
text:
I must preface this with the fact that I got this before our first snowfall, so I can't really report on how it performs. But I can give feedback on what the unit entails, especially in comparison to two other battery  snowblowers I have.
I'll Start with the CONS: First,This item came with (2) batteries, and I had hopes that it would use both batteries, but the sneaky engineers created a place for both batteries but can only use one. The other slot is just for storage. With only 40v on hand, and a single battery, even at 4ah, I don't think this will get very far. 
Secondly, according to the manual, the expected usage is one hour of use, but the battery takes 2 hours to charge. 
Third, while the scraper bar is removable, which is nice, it is plastic and I'd imagine that this will wear away very quickly. 
Fourth, there is no speed control. It is only on or off. And the start button is on the side in a weird spot. I think it will be tough while you are wearing gloves. 
Fifth, the paddle does not go the width of the opening. there is a good 3-4 inches on either side that is just open and might clog up, or just not get flung out, effectively narrowing the unit.
Lastly, it is a very light machine in weight. That's nice to push around, but I don't know how long this will hold up, as it is mostly plastic and we'll see how well it lasts. 
On the PRO side: It is lightweight and easy to push around. 
Second, the rotation mechanism is fairly direct and easy to use. 
Last, the safety controls are easy to hold onto and the cross bar is at a good height.

productName: Cordless 40-volt 20-in Single-stage Push Battery Snow Blower (Battery Included) (Charger Included)
title: Light Snow Thrower for Small Paved Driveway
text:
This snow "thrower" is designed for small, paved driveways or areas. I was able to clear about a 30x35' area of 5" of snow per battery. Deeper snow will reduce the area you can clear. It was easy to assemble with a 3/8" and 10mm socket in about 10 minutes. At about 35# it's easy to lift and move around. It is not self propelled, so you have to push it through the snow and the handle is short forcing my 6'2" frame to stoop over while using it. It did throw the snow 15-20', so from the center of the driveway, most of the snow landed off the driveway. The shoot rotation control is quick and easy to rotate from side to side.

I did try using it on an area of gravel driveway and it tended to dig into the gravel and shoot it out. I saw no damage to the paddles, but I doubt that it would hold up to long term use over gravel. It was challenging to hold the front edge up above the gravel and I ended up with a bit over an inch of snow remaining. 

My biggest complaint with this unit is the batteries. They will not charge if they are too cold or hot. When I first received the unit and tried to charge the batteries they were at 35 degrees from being outside. It took them over an hour and a half to warm up in the 70 degree house before they would start charging. Then after discharging fully in about 10 minutes, they were hot and took about two hours to cool down enough in the 70 degree house to start the charging cycle. Charging took just over the stated 120 minutes to charge each battery. So if you discharge both batteries using it for 20 minutes, it will be over six hours before you have two recharged batteries to continue with.

productName: Cordless 40-volt 20-in Single-stage Push Battery Snow Blower (Battery Included) (Charger Included)
title: Badger Snowblower
text: I unpacked it and set everything out. I was surprised at the amount of plastic parts. My biggest concern is how they will hold up when the weather gets below zero. Will they become brittle and break? We will find out this winter. The auger is made of hard rubber. The shoot is manually adjusted, and has several adjustment settings. On the bottom of the blower is a set of plastic high points. The blower does not get to ground level because of these high points. The batteries charge pretty quick, about 4 hours per battery. It comes with a charger and two batteries. I will see how the really cold weather treats the machine and its parts. If anything changes, I will add to the review this coming spring.

productName: Cordless 40-volt 20-in Single-stage Push Battery Snow Blower (Battery Not Included) (Charger Included)
title: Okay for small jobs and those who hate to shovel.
text:
This snow thrower was easy to assemble in 10-15 minutes and is made of good quality material like the heavy-duty rubber blades, brushless motor and surprisingly high-end features like a remote-chute handle, LED headlight, 8-inch rear wheels. For uninhibited start-ups the 40 volt battery should be stored indoors in cold environments.  While it is sold as a 20-inch snow thrower it actually will only clear a 12-inch width, which is as wide as the augers inside the mouth of the housing.  The battery lasted about 20-25 minutes. 
Best for use in light to medium snow conditions, for clearing an average walkway or small driveway.  Okay for a quick pass through, but the battery won't last much beyond that.  You can invest in a second battery to buy yourself a bit more time.

productName: Cordless 40-volt 20-in Single-stage Push Battery Snow Blower (Battery Not Included) (Charger Included)
title: Battery one stage = low power, short throw
text: I really want to like all battery powered tools. I even have a battery Miter Saw... But this is my third battery powered snow blower and they all lack throwing power. If you just need this to clear sidewalks, then this may be a great option. But I also have a large driveway and this unit only demonstrates a throw range of about 3 to 4 feet. My second issue is that this item arrived broken out of the box and was not due to shipping damage. The ring that directs snow up the chute was detached on one side, and as it was designed, is not reparable without a complete disassembly, so self service is not likely. If the bolt to hold the assembly was reachable from the outside, it would not have broken the way it did. It is possible it was damaged while packing as it is a likely place to want to grab the unit from the front while boxing. This unit has a single battery, but has storage for a second under the lid. It is relatively light, under 50 pounds, while still being heavy enough not to slide away easily on icy walkways and dig into the snow. The chute angle adjustment must be made at the chute, but it throws so close, that it is unlikely to make a difference other than in windy weather. As you can see in the video, it was blowing right back at the camera-person. The chute is hard to adjust at the extreme ends of the arc and I felt like I might break the gears if I pushed to hard. I suggest using a socket wrench with extension for assembly and ensure you read the directions first to know where all the pieces go. I made several mistaken assumptions my first time through until I read the manual.  The light is a nice feature, but not terribly bright. The only controls are the safety bar and the push to start button. I would much prefer an on/off switch and the safety bar so that adjusting the chute and restarting did not take so long. I'm sure this is just a safety requirement, but still slows down the process of getting the snow moved.

title: Leaks fuel from the reservoir
text: I used the trimmer very few times, and it has some problems which are annoying but tolerable, and one problem which makes the tool dangerous. It is always a struggle to start it initially. Once it finally starts, it is then pretty easy to stop and start it again. Unfortunately, it is necessary to stop and start it several times because the string line head does not work properly. It has two chambers, and one of them runs out of the line much faster than the other. After few minutes of trimming, there is a string coming out of only one hole, not both. This is because one chamber is already empty. So, it takes to stop the trimmer, remove the head and rewind the line. Rewinding is very easy though, this part is designed well. These problems are tolerable, but there is also a problem with fuel leaking badly from under the reservoir cap. Sometimes I need to turn the tool 90 degrees to edge the grass, and this causes the fuel to start leaking. The leak is not small, it will empty the reservoir in just few seconds. Considering that the unit gets hot almost immediately after it starts, this leak can easily cause it to catch fire. Unfortunately, the part list is nowhere to be found. There is a phony link on the HD page reading "Replacement Part List", but the link opens a PDF file which has only one page, instructing to send email to customer support. I need to find a way to buy the new reservoir or the cap, but it is not possible to be sure that the replacement will work without knowing the part number. I wish that the manufacturer of this trimmer had a more reliable cap to close the reservoir so it does not leak. After all, I used the tool very few times, and it already has this nasty problem.

title: DO NOT PURCHASE!
text:
I ordered this online from Home Depot. Home Depot is great! Fast delivery. However: THIS PRODUCT IS TERRIBLE! Upon delivery, I couldn’t assemble it properly due to terrible instructions included that actually show a part THAT DOES NOT EVEN EXIST and if it did would make the unit unusable! I had to go on YouTube for an assembly video. Upon completion, it ran for about ten minutes and the trimmer line broke TWICE while trimming just grass! I am familiar with trimmers, avoid hitting the fence and other objects, and I have used them for many years. I’m not a rookie! Respooling the line was not too difficult but two line failures in ten minutes is not acceptable! The vibrations are excessive! So excessive that the spring loaded pin that positions the lower shaft into the upper shaft is shaken out of its position causing the trimmer head to rotate clockwise out of position despite the hand screw designed to hold the shaft in position (along with the spring loaded pin) being tightened very tight. After several re-assemblies of the lower shaft for this issue, I called Wild Badger customer support and was asked to re-assemble it again for the agent. It failed again. I had to send pictures and was told that a new unit would be sent. It never arrived. The new unit was actually delivered to a different state and different address according to the tracking information. Wild Badger says that the unit is not returnable to them or to Home Depot! Not true! After the new unit did not arrive, a call to Home Depot appeared to solve the issue. They said to drain the gasoline and return it to the store and they would send a new unit with a courtesy discount. Like I said, Home Depot is great!!! The new unit arrived, was assembled, started easily, and worked FOR LESS THAN TEN MINUTES before the same issues started again. Thinking I may have done something wrong, I watched a different YouTube assembly video and re-assembled the unit. (I actually hadn’t done anything incorrectly with the assembly of either unit!) Upon starting it again, the same line break and head rotation occurred. JUST DON’T BUY THIS MACHINE! 
I will be returning this unit to Home Depot today and selecting a different brand.
